summary: LEGION-25 Part B (legion controller start, the operator-launched controller for runtime: kubernetes) on pull request #1110, tested at branch head e82da69112b42591365b11011700c923e5adbb43 (the implementer's code head 58785d9a plus its handoff commit; the code is identical). The implementer's proof reproduces exactly: 16/16 in the CLI test file, 4/4 secret-route round trips, and the three real-binary refusals byte for byte. My own end-to-end drove the real `legion controller start` binary against a real loopback `startLegionApi` with a fake `omp` that dumps what it was launched with, then replayed the plugin's /controller/ready by hand and read the state page: the secret is fetched with the operator bearer, written 0600 under a 0700 secrets/, the gh shim 0700 and legion launcher 0755 installed, one joined --append-system-prompt of role prompt + deployment instructions, the exact controller environment with no raw secret in it, Oh My Pi's exit code passed through, --daemon-url (trailing slash stripped) overriding the file; /controller/ready records {runtime:kubernetes, external:true, sessionId, registeredAt}, ignores the reported ompSessionFile, never calls stashControllerReady, and the state page parses under LegionDaemonApi.State.response at contract 6; a second start kills the old secret (403) and the new one works (200). The Envoy-backed probe over a real loopback HTTP listener is alive at a last_seen age of 239 999 ms and gone at exactly 240 000 ms, gone for another holder, unknown on 401 and on an unreachable listener, and leaves the record in state. Spec Acceptance 3-7 all hold against code and tests; tmux behaviour is unchanged (the controller pane-env pin and the runtime contract suite pass; the branch's only tmux-facing edits are the controllerLaunch rename, ControllerLocator parameter widening, and a reworded refusal); docs, skill, example, and manifests are present and the example itself passes the strict loader; contract 6 on the branch, main still at 5; ProcessManager reads no locator shape. Full suites green locally (daemon 1665/0/14 skip, contracts 120, pi-envoy 187, tsc clean x3, biome clean) and CI green at e82da691. No failures. The kind check is BLOCKED-BY-ORDER and was not run.

implementerProof.how: Re-ran every command the implementer recorded at the same code (head e82da691 = 58785d9a + .legion/implement.json): `cd packages/daemon && bun test src/cli/__tests__/controller-start.test.ts` -> 16 pass / 0 fail; `bun test src/daemon/__tests__/api.test.ts -t "controller/secret"` -> 4 pass / 0 fail; the real binary `bun src/cli/index.ts controller start` with no --config -> `Usage: legion controller start --config <controller.yaml> [--daemon-url <url>]` exit 1; a 0644 token file -> `operator_token_file <path> is readable by its group or others (mode 0644); chmod 0600 it` exit 1; a 0600 file with daemon_url http://127.0.0.1:1 -> `could not reach the Legion daemon at http://127.0.0.1:1: Unable to connect. Is the computer able to access the url?; is the port-forward running? (never falls back to another address)` exit 1 — each message byte for byte what the handoff's proof[0] records. Full suites re-run: daemon 1665 pass / 14 skip / 0 fail across 69 files, contracts 120, pi-envoy 187, `bunx tsc --noEmit` exit 0 in all three packages, `bunx biome check src/` clean — the same counts proof[2] records. The handoff carried a well-formed four-entry proof array with commands, observations, head SHA, and negative controls; proof[3] correctly records the kind check as BLOCKED-BY-ORDER rather than claiming it.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 3: legion controller start launches the controller on the operator's machine with LEGION_CONTROLLER, LEGION_CONTROLLER_SECRET_FILE (fetched via POST /legion/v1/controller/secret), LEGION_DAEMON_URL; the files and modes it writes; the exact command and environment; the plugin's /controller/ready records the external record and the state page admits it.
proof.surface: The real `legion controller start` binary (`bun src/cli/index.ts controller start`) driven as a subprocess from an operator-like environment (no LEGION_*/DISPATCH_*/ENVOY_*/*_KEY names passed in) against a real loopback `startLegionApi` server started in-process with operatorToken set — the same in-process API api.test.ts starts, no daemon process, tmux, NATS, or rig (Sami's 2026-09-13 19:00Z order) — with `omp_invocation` pointed at a fake `omp` shell script that records its argv and environment and exits 7. Throwaway script /tmp/legion25-tester-jlALZ4/e2e.ts, not committed.
proof.command: bun /tmp/legion25-tester-jlALZ4/e2e.ts — inside it: `bun src/cli/index.ts controller start --config <dir>/controller-e2e.yaml --daemon-url http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` (the file's daemon_url deliberately http://127.0.0.1:1; state_dir ./state; instructions ./instructions.md; omp_launch_prefix [env, FAKE_PREFIX=1]); then `POST /legion/v1/controller/ready {secret:<written file>, sessionId:'ses_operator', ompSessionFile:'/laptop/omp/session.jsonl'}` and `GET /legion/v1/state` parsed with LegionDaemonApi.State.response.
proof.observed: Exit 7 (the fake omp's code) after one `[legion] starting the controller for demo against http://127.0.0.1:<port>; state in <dir>/state` line. Written: state/secrets/ 0700, state/secrets/legion-demo-controller 0600 holding a UUID, state/worker-bin/gh 0700, state/bin/legion 0755, state/deployment-instructions.md starting `# Deployment instructions (demo)`; state.controllerCapabilityHash rotated. The fake omp ran with cwd <dir>/state/controller and argv `--append-system-prompt <1079 chars: controller-root.md, blank line, the instructions file>` (env consumed the prefix), and its environment carried exactly LEGION_CONTROLLER=1, LEGION_ROLE=controller, LEGION_DAEMON_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port> (the --daemon-url value, trailing slash stripped, the file's value overridden), LEGION_PROJECT=demo, LEGION_STATE_DIR, ENVOY_NATS_URL=nats://a:4222,nats://b:4222, ENVOY_URL, PATH=<state>/worker-bin:<state>/bin:<operator PATH>, GH_CONFIG_DIR=<state>/gh, GH_TOKEN= GITHUB_TOKEN= GH_HOST= (empty), LEGION_GRANT_FILE=<state>/secrets/legion-demo-controller-grant, DISPATCH_URL=https://dispatch.test (trailing slash normalised), DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE and ENVOY_TOKEN_FILE pointing at the operator's own files, LEGION_CONTROLLER_SECRET_FILE=<state>/secrets/legion-demo-controller — and no LEGION_CONTROLLER_SECRET, ENVOY_TOKEN, or DISPATCH_TOKEN value. /controller/ready with the written secret -> 200, state.roles[legion-demo-controller]={role:controller, sessionId:ses_operator}, state.controllerLocator={runtime:kubernetes, external:true, sessionId:ses_operator, registeredAt:<now>} with no ompSessionFile, stashControllerReady never called, the onControllerReady (forced resync) hook ran; GET /legion/v1/state returned that record field for field and the whole page parsed under LegionDaemonApi.State.response (contract 6). A second `controller start` wrote a different secret; /controller/ready with the old secret -> 403, with the new -> 200 and the record moved to the new session (last claim wins).
proof.negativeControl: Controls the implementer did not use: (1) a blank operator token file (0600, whitespace only) -> `operator_token_file names <path>/blank-token, which is empty`, exit 1, nothing fetched or written; (2) `operator_token_file: ~/operator-token-0600` -> resolved literally under the config directory, `operator_token_file names <dir>/~/operator-token-0600, which could not be read: ENOENT ...` (tilde is not expanded, as the loader documents); (3) two unknown keys (`runtime: kubernetes`, `bind: 0.0.0.0`) -> both named in one message joined by `; `, each pointing at deploy/kubernetes/daemon/controller.yaml.example; (4) `--daemon-url http://127.0.0.1:1/` -> the trailing slash is stripped before use (`could not reach the Legion daemon at http://127.0.0.1:1`); `--daemon-url 'not a url'` -> `--daemon-url must be a valid URL`; (5) a wrong operator token through the real CLI against the real loopback API -> exit 1 `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/legion/v1/controller/secret answered 403: Invalid operator token — the operator token does not match the daemon's operator_token_file, or this daemon has none configured`, controllerCapabilityHash unchanged, exactly one daemon log line `[legion] refused POST /legion/v1/controller/secret: wrong operator token`; (6) the shipped deploy/kubernetes/daemon/controller.yaml.example itself passes the strict loader and fails only at its missing ./operator-token. In every refusal ~/.local/state/legion/demo-controller was never created.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 4: in runtime: kubernetes the daemon never launches the controller and controllerAlive reads the controller role's Envoy holder and last_seen; the liveness window is max(worker_boot_timeout_seconds, 2 x 120 s).
proof.surface: The real KubernetesRuntime (constructed with an unused Kubernetes client — the external-record probe never touches it) probing the external record recorded by the /controller/ready above, over a real loopback HTTP listener (in-process Bun.serve answering GET /v1/roles/legion-demo-controller with a fixed clock) — the same throwaway script; plus `bun test src/daemon/__tests__/processes.test.ts -t controller` (38 pass, 1 LEGION_TMUX_LIVE skip) for ensureController under FakeRuntime({controllerLaunch:'operator'}).
proof.command: bun /tmp/legion25-tester-jlALZ4/e2e.ts (section 5) at workerBootTimeoutMs 120000; `cd packages/daemon && bun test src/daemon/__tests__/processes.test.ts -t controller`; `bun test src/daemon/__tests__/runtime-kubernetes.test.ts -t operator-launched` (11 pass).
proof.observed: controllerLivenessMs(120000)=240000. last_seen age 0 ms -> {status:alive}; 239 999 ms -> alive; 240 000 ms -> {status:dead, reason:gone} with `[legion] the controller session ses_operator_2 was last seen 240s ago; treating it as gone`; 240 001 ms -> gone. The request carried `Authorization: Bearer envoy-bearer` to /v1/roles/legion-demo-controller. Another holder -> gone with `the controller role is held by session ses_someone_else, not the recorded ses_operator_2`. The record stayed in state after every dead/unknown verdict. processes.test.ts: three ensureController calls inside one worker_boot_timeout_seconds interval log exactly one `[legion] controller not registered; run legion controller start`, a fourth after the interval logs a second; zero mints, zero spawns, no controllerLocator, no registration-deadline sleep; a live external record silences the log; recordControllerReady replaces the record (last claim wins) and re-arms the log, and is false under a daemon-launched runtime.
proof.negativeControl: The listener answering 401 (wrong daemon bearer) -> {status:unknown}, `[legion] Envoy listener http://127.0.0.1:<port> answered 401 to the controller role lookup`, nothing cleared; the listener stopped -> {status:unknown}, `... unreachable while probing the controller: Unable to connect...`, record left in state — never a death verdict, so no spawn and no cleared locator (the spec's `Envoy unreachable -> unknown` row).

The tmux harness refuses the external record in probe/connect/stop with the reworded message (runtime.contract.test.ts). blockedByOrder: Sami, 2026-09-13 19:00Z (no smoke rig, scratch daemon, kind cluster, or throwaway NATS): the spec's Acceptance 3 kind check was not run and no stand-in was built. The command, recorded verbatim from the implementer's handoff for when the order lifts: `kubectl -n legion port-forward svc/legion-daemon-demo 13370:13370 & legion controller start --config deploy/kubernetes/daemon/controller.yaml.example --daemon-url http://127.0.0.1:13370`, then `legion state --json` showing controllerLocator {runtime:"kubernetes", external:true, sessionId, registeredAt} and a triage notice reaching that terminal; its negative controls: a wrong OPERATOR_TOKEN (exit non-zero naming the URL, 403), the port-forward closed (exit non-zero naming the URL), the terminal closed (the daemon logs `controller not registered; run legion controller start` once per interval). Also not renderable here: `kubectl kustomize deploy/kubernetes/daemon/overlays/kind` (no kubectl or kustomize on this box); the four changed manifests were instead parsed as YAML and the operator mount -> volume -> legion.yaml path chain checked structurally.
observations: Under an operator-launched runtime, controllerAlive() maps a probe verdict of `unknown` (Envoy unreachable, a non-2xx, an unreadable body) to false, so ensureController falls through to the rate-limited `[legion] controller not registered; run legion controller start` line right after the probe's own `Envoy listener ... unreachable while probing the controller` line. The behaviour is the spec's (no spawn, nothing cleared, retried on the next wake) — only the second line's wording is imprecise in that one case. Not a defect; a wording candidate for a fast-follow.

The PR body names `pi-legion-envoy-v1.35.0` as the likely first release declaring contract 6, hedged with `unless another plugin release lands first`; main has since released 1.35.0 and 1.35.1 at contract 5, so the release cut from the merge commit will carry a later version. The hedge covers it; the merger's READY packet should name the actual tag.
